articles.title: Championship roundup: Zemura seals Watford reprieve for Dionisi
articles.summary: Watford out of bottom three after beating Charlton 2-0. Middlesbrough 2-2 Cardiff; Millwall 2-2 Lincoln. Watford lifted the pressure on Alessio Dionisi and quelled their supporters’ rebellion against the owner, Gino Pozzo, with a deserved 2-0 win against a sluggish Charlton side.
body: After shipping nine goals in calamitous defeats by Burnley and Cardiff, Dionisi’s side had slumped into the bottom three and the fans had turned their anger on Pozzo. But goals from Luca Kjerrumgaard and the substitute Jordan Zemura – the Zimbabwe defender’s first for the club – extended Charlton’s worrying run to eight games without a win as the Addicks were booed off at Vicarage Road.

Despite the mood of insurrection swirling around Pozzo on social media, protests against his 14-year ownership outside the ground before kick-off were limited and Watford kept their first clean sheet in 210 days with only their second win in three months.

Jake Cooper’s scrambled equaliser rescued a point for Millwall as they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Lincoln. The Imps looked on course to put Wednesday’s 6-0 home thrashing against West Ham behind them in style when goals from Andrei Coubiș and Rob Street put them in a strong position after 33 minutes at the Den. There was some controversy around the second goal, though, as what looked a clear handball by Reeco Hackett in the buildup was missed by the assistant stood close by.

articles.title: Glasgow get bonus-point win at emotion-filled Sale
articles.summary: Glasgow Warriors pull away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup at an emotional CorpAcq Stadium.
body: Pre-match tears were shed on the pitch and in the stands during a minute's silence in memory of former Sale lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday at the Johannesburg Lions' team hotel ahead of their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.
The 31-year-old played regularly for Sale last season, and his former side started positively as they sought a memorable performance.
Ben Curry peeled off a maul and sprinted through, much to Glasgow's surprise, before Arron Reed crossed out wide after some sharp handling.
However, a penalty try for a maul infringement sent Gus Warr to the sin-bin, before Tom Roebuck joined him after tripping Warriors captain Kyle Steyn.

articles.title: The right is pushing its anti-trans fury on the WNBA. Players and fans are loudly pushing back
articles.summary: As the WNBA finals kick off Saturday in San Francisco, the pro-LGBTQ+ sports fanbase push a message of inclusion in the face of anti-trans attacks. Sign up for WNBA 30: a free women’s basketball newsletter.
body: At Wilka’s Sports Bar in lower Manhattan, a crowd of mostly LGBTQ+ fans was fired up during a WNBA playoff game between the New York Liberty and the Atlanta Dream. When the Liberty’s Jonquel Jones blocked the Dream’s star forward Angel Reese at the basket, then chest-bumped her – leading teammates to separate them – the bar erupted in cheers. One fan quietly joked: “Now kiss!”
“I love strong women, and I love supporting strong women,” said August, a trans organizer and Liberty fan who asked to go by their first name for privacy reasons.

The scene at Wilka’s, where a sign reading “trans people belong in sports” hangs prominently behind the bar, exemplifies much of the WNBA fanbase, which, like the league itself, is heavily queer. But many wouldn’t know that from reading recent headlines about the league. Since the summer, the WNBA has become the target of rightwing activists pushing their agenda to ban trans women and girls from sports. The league has no explicit rule barring or permitting trans women and there are no trans women in the WNBA.

articles.title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injury
articles.summary: Chelsea have returned from the international break with an authority that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. Two goals from Pedro Neto condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as the visitors climbed to fourth on the back of their first Premier League clean sheet since January.
body: There were goalkeeping problems at both ends, with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in succession as David Moyes’ side suffered self-inflicted wounds. But Everton could have no complaints about the merits of Chelsea’s victory given their contrasting performances in the second half.

There was more needle than quality on display in a first half that Everton edged and they could question why they were still facing 11 men by half-time. Morgan Rogers risked a second yellow card when leaping into a challenge with James Garner shortly before the break. The Chelsea forward caught the ball and the man but, beyond both players feeling the impact of the 50-50, there was no further punishment from Paul Tierney.

Rogers’s tackle was just as reckless as the one that brought an earlier booking for Harrison Armstrong, one of five yellows shown in a half that owed its entertainment to the animosity between the teams. The hosts’ grievance deepened when Rogers played a part in Neto’s breakthrough moments after the restart.

articles.title: Chacarra leads as McIlroy fades before play halted
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra extends his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy loses ground before the third round is halted because of darkness.
body: Eugenio Chacarra extended his lead at the DP World India Championship but Rory McIlroy lost ground before the third round was halted because of darkness.
Spain's Chacarra led by one shot at 10 under after two rounds at the weather-hit event at Delhi Golf Club and sits two clear after 11 holes of his third round.

After successive rounds of 67, the 26-year-old birdied four of his opening seven holes to cement his place at the top as he bids to replace American Patrick Reed at the summit of the season-long Race to Dubai rankings.
Fellow Spaniard Angel Hidalgo and the Netherlands' Joost Luisten are his closest challengers at 12 under, with Scotland's Scott Jamieson a shot further back.

Robert Griffin III believes the Georgia Bulldogs remain the SEC’s standard after their 20-17 road victory over the Alabama Crimson Tide.
body: Georgia’s Week 6 win over Alabama strengthened the team’s position in the SEC race and marked Kirby Smart ’s first regular-season win vs. the Crimson Tide.

The former Heisman Trophy winner shared his assessment Friday night on X, formerly Twitter, calling Georgia the conference’s bully and the best team in the country. His endorsement came six days after the Bulldogs won in Tuscaloosa and ahead of Saturday’s home matchup against Auburn.
“Yes, they’re still the bullies of the SEC. They’re the kings of the SEC, and Georgia destroyed Alabama’s Death Star.”

The Bulldogs delivered a balanced performance October 10 at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Ranked No. 2 entering the matchup, Georgia outgained No. 6 Alabama 455-346 to improve to 6-0 overall and 4-0 in SEC play.

articles.title: McIlroy drops out of contention at DP World India Championship
articles.summary: Spain's Eugenio Chacarra holds the lead at the DP World India Championship with Rory McIlroy dropping out of contention after play was suspended for the day on Saturday.
body: Chacarra was leading by two strokes on 14 under when Saturday's play was suspended because of fading light, with most of the field yet to finish their third round.
The Spaniard was four under for his round after 11 holes, having started out in the halfway lead after completing a second-round 67 early Saturday.
Joost Luiten was four under after 12 holes and Angel Hidalgo four under after 11 holes, with both players tied for second place on 12 under par.
Daniel Hillier, Adrian Meronk and Scott Jamieson were a further shot back.

articles.summary: Barcelona’s extraordinary start to the 2026-27 season has earned widespread praise, with the Catalan club looking unstoppable across all competitions. body: According to SPORT, Abella, who currently works on Fiorentina’s coaching staff, praised Barcelona’s playing style in an interview with Flashscore ahead of the Catalans’ meeting with Real Betis.
“Alongside PSG and Bayern, they are the team I enjoy watching most right now,” Abella said.
He highlighted Barcelona’s ability to play at tremendous speed without abandoning the technical principles that have traditionally defined the club.
The former defender particularly admired their aggressive defending, willingness to take risks and ability to combine entertaining football with efficiency.

articles.title: Almeraq proves his class in British Champions Sprint
articles.summary: Almeraq confirmed himself as this season’s star sprinter with a third top-level triumph of the campaign in the Qatar Racing British Champions Sprint Stakes at Ascot.
body: William and Maureen Haggas celebrated further success with their star sprinter Almeraq, who chased down Paborus to strike in the Qatar Racing British Champions Sprint Stakes under Tom Marquand.

After coming out on top in a thrilling Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot, William Haggas' 11-10 favourite bounced back from July Cup disappointment with a blistering display in the Sprint Cup on very soft ground at Haydock.

With conditions not as testing this time, the four-year-old - who was involved in a horrific fall at York that ultimately ended Jim Crowley's riding career a little over a year ago - showed all of his class and versatility in the hands of Tom Marquand.
He answered every urging from his rider to hit top gear close home and run down Ed Bethell's Paborus for a neck success. Completing a one-three for the Somerville Lodge was Division.
